# v1.1.0-dev.71 — WLM was enforcing a limit that doesn't exist

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.70`.

Eighteen research claims from two releases ago were never
independently checked, because that pass ran out of budget partway
through. They have been checked now. Nine were wrong, and two had
already turned into shipped bugs.

## Registering A Resolution Refused Sizes That Would Have Worked

dev.66 added a check that stopped you registering a resolution
outside what Parsec's driver advertises. The point was to stop you
spending an administrator prompt and one of only two slots on
something hopeless.

The driver doesn't have that limit.

Someone took Parsec's display driver apart to check. It reads the
resolutions you register, confirms each number is present, and
appends them. There is no range check anywhere in it. The numbers
WLM was enforcing describe the driver's own built-in list, which is
a different thing entirely.

So it says something now instead of refusing:

```
5120 × 1440 @ 60 Hz is outside it. Parsec's built-in list stops at
4096 pixels on the long side. It may still work. The driver does
not check.
```

Your call, not WLM's.

## And It Refused Rotated Screens Outright

Worse, and nobody spotted this until the machine was measured
directly. The check compared width against width. A rotated display
lists its resolutions the other way round, so **every single one of
a portrait monitor's own resolutions failed the check**. All
ninety-one of them.

Clicking **Add resolutions** on a portrait screen filled the row
with that screen's largest size, and Register then refused it while
announcing a height limit smaller than the monitor you were looking
at.

It compares the long and short sides now. A rotated size is the same
size.

## "Add The Sizes Your Profiles Ask For" Had The Same Bug

It compared a wanted size against a rotated screen's list without
accounting for the rotation. So it offered to register resolutions
your display already had. That is an administrator prompt and one of
your two slots spent on nothing.

The resolution picker was fixed for exactly this a few releases
back. The fix never reached this button.

## USB Mobile Monitor Does Take Custom Sizes

WLM told you that driver ships a fixed list. Its own installer
writes ten user-definable slots, which is five times what Parsec
offers. The "60 Hz only" half was right.

## A Driver Named Without Spaces Read As A Real Monitor

Found while measuring rather than by any of the eighteen. WLM spots
an unfamiliar virtual display by looking for whole words like
"virtual" in the driver name. That is deliberate, so a real monitor
called something like "Virtualis" cannot trip it.

A driver named `VirtualDisplayDriver`, with no spaces, has no whole
words to find. It was being treated as a physical monitor, which
loses every piece of virtual-display handling at once.

## Also Corrected

Written up in the research notes rather than changing behaviour:
a virtual display's stored monitor data is readable even when it's
unplugged, Windows checks both size and refresh rate the same way,
and the "unsafe modes" flag people reach for is neither documented
away nor harmless. WLM still won't touch it.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
